text: Nucleosomes, the fundamental units of chromatin, regulate transcription, replication and repair. H3(T118) phosphorylation [H3(T118ph)], prepared by expressed protein ligation, reduces DNA-histone binding by 2 kcal/mol, increases nucleosome mobility 28-fold, and raises DNA accessibility near the dyad 6-fold. It also accelerates hMSH2-hMSH6 nucleosome disassembly and enables SWI/SNF-mediated disassembly, suggesting it reprograms remodeling. Heterochromatin—marked by H3K9 methylation and bound by conserved HP1 proteins—mediates gene silencing and sister-chromatid cohesion. Phosphorylation of fission-yeast HP1 homolog Swi6 differentially regulates transcriptional effectors, altering heterochromatic transcription without affecting cohesion. ATP-dependent SNF2/SWI2-family remodelers increase nucleosome mobility. The Saccharomyces cerevisiae INO80 complex (~12 polypeptides, including two bacterial RuvB-related helicases) remodels chromatin, facilitates in vitro transcription, displays 3'→5' DNA helicase activity; ino80 mutants are hypersensitive to DNA-damaging agents.
